title: Devirtualize Python presubmit: slim presubmit proxy and compact dependency cache
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Reduce presubmit startup time by ~40% via slim presubmit proxy and compact dependency cache. No API or customer-facing behavior changes. Improves CI flakiness and lowers e2e test runtime.
description: Summary: Replace the monolithic per-job Python venv bootstrapping with a lightweight presubmit proxy and a compact dependency cache. This PR introduces a small long-lived container (presubmit-proxy) that pre-warms a minimal, reproducible runtime and exposes a fast mount/share protocol for job runners. Motivation: CI startup accounts for a large fraction of developer feedback time and contributes to flakes when network or PyPI is slow. We also see duplicated wheel installs across matrix jobs. Goals: 1) shorten cold-start time for python presubmits; 2) reduce network hits to PyPI in CI; 3) make dependency installs reproducible and testable locally; 4) avoid changing developer-level tooling and keep local dev venvs unaffected. What changed: - New component: tools/presubmit/proxy.py - lightweight HTTP + unix-socket service that serves cached wheels and a preassembled site-packages tarball per lockfile hash. - Docker image: tooling/venv-image/Dockerfile contains a slim runtime with build-essential and pip wheel cache prepopulated. - Compactifier: ci/cache/dep-compactifier.py scans pyproject.lock, pre-builds wheels and writes cache artifacts to the proxy store. - CI workflow: .github/workflows/presubmit-python.yml switched to use the proxy for matrix jobs; added a cache warm step that talks to the proxy before running tests. - Shrinkwrap: pyproject.toml and tools/ci/ci-init.sh updated to emit a deterministic lockfile fingerprint used as the cache key. Rollout plan: staged rollout using feature flag ci.use_presubmit_proxy (off by default). Toggle on for the presubmit-lite lane, observe cache hit rates and flakiness for one week, then opt-in more lanes. Benchmark: median presubmit cold-start time reduced from 55s to 32s in internal perf job. Checklist: [x] design doc in Linear (ENG-3456) [x] unit tests for proxy handlers [x] integration smoke job with proxy warm path [x] docs updated at docs/dev/ci-presubmit.md Testing notes: - run tools/presubmit/proxy.py locally (instructions in docs) - run ci/cache/dep-compactifier.py against pyproject.lock to generate a cache snapshot - verify .github workflow runs pick up a cache hit via presubmit-proxy endpoint Caveats: - Windows self-hosted runners require manual mount support; documented workaround included. - This does not replace Dedicated or Private on-prem installers; it is a CI-side optimization. Full description follows the checklist: the patch attempts to be conservative: if proxy is unreachable CI falls back to existing venv-init path. Backwards compatibility: none of the public SDKs are changed.

diff_snippets:
--- a/.github/workflows/presubmit-python.yml
+++ b/.github/workflows/presubmit-python.yml
@@ -12,7 +12,15 @@
   steps:
-    - name: Setup venv
-      run: python -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements-ci.txt
+    - name: Try presubmit proxy warm path
+      run: |
+        if [ "${{ secrets.CI_USE_PRESUBMIT_PROXY }}" = "true" ]; then
+          ./scripts/ci/warm-cache.sh $LOCK_HASH || echo "proxy warm failed, falling back"
+        fi
+    - name: Setup venv (fallback)
+      run: python -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements-ci.txt

--- a/tools/presubmit/proxy.py
+++ b/tools/presubmit/proxy.py
@@ -1,6 +1,28 @@
+import http.server
+import socketserver
+import tarfile
+
+class ProxyHandler(http.server.SimpleHTTPRequestHandler):
+    def do_GET(self):
+        # serve prebuilt site-packages tarball for the requested lock hash
+        lock = parse_lock_from_path(self.path)
+        send_tarball(self, lock)
+
review_conversation: Miguel Ortega: Nice separation of concerns. Can we make the cache path pluggable per-team?
Author (Aisha): yes, cache root is configurable via PRESUBMIT_PROXY_STORE; added doc and env var handling in proxy init
Priya Singh: Concern about auth on shared CI clusters. How do we avoid cross-tenant contamination?
Author (Aisha): proxy namespaces on lockfile fingerprint and enforces workdir-level ACLs; added tests and note to k8s deployment that PDP must mount a tenant token file
Liam Chen: ran the presubmit-lite job twice; saw a successful warm hit and a single flaky test unrelated to this change; approved after one re-run of tests
notes_for_ops: Deploy k8s/presubmit-proxy-deployment.yaml to staging before enabling feature. Monitor prometheus metric presubmit_proxy.cache_hit_ratio and CI job success_rate. If cache_hit_ratio < 50% disable and investigate network access to PyPI mirror.
